newsitem.title: USA: Judge orders O.J. Simpson to turn over property.
newsitem.headline: Judge orders O.J. Simpson to turn over property.

text.p: A judge ordered O.J. Simpson to turn over his Heisman Trophy, art, jewels and other items worth more than $400,000 to satisfy part of the civil award against him, according to court papers released on Thursday.

A civil jury in February found Simpson liable for the deaths of his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman, awarding $33.5 million in damages to the estate of Nicole Brown, and Goldman's parents, Fred Goldman and Sharon Rufo.
Superior Court Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki made the order this week after Fred Goldman submitted a list of more than 100 items he wanted turned over to the court to prevent Simpson from selling them.
Fujisaki ordered Simpson to surrender the property to the sheriff's department, and "let the parties fight it out," over who gets what.
In his order, Fujisaki gave Simpson seven days from the time he was served with the notice to turn over the property.

Simpson lawyer Phil Baker said he would serve his client with the papers as soon as possible but also noted that "99 percent" of the items listed no longer belonged to Simpson and had been assigned to a trust for his two young children and other unidentified third parties.

The items Simpson was ordered to turn over include several pieces of football memorabilia, including the Heisman Trophy, a Buffalo Bills football helmet, four football jerseys, and 10 commemorative footballs.

Also listed in the court papers were a number of art works in the likeness of Simpson including an Andy Warhol silkscreen entitled "O.J. Simpson", a metal sculpture of the former football star and a large photograph.
Simpson was also ordered to turn over several Tiffany lamps, jewels, glassware, a 1996 Chevrolet Suburban and framed congratulatory letters from Richard Nixon.
